description: CCRL-Blitz-anchored opponent pool for Sgurr calibration. Names must match fastchess PGN tags exactly. Anchors are the ccrl_blitz values below; the solve reads this pool's games and pool-E's, which were played under identical conditions.

book.why: Generic and engine-neutral, within CCRL's 12-moves-per-side limit. Unchanged from pool-D.

engines.name: Bitfox-2.5.0
engines.build: bitfox.exe from bitfox-2.5.0-windows-x86_64.zip (zip matches its published sha256)

engines.name: Lynx-1.11.0
engines.build: Lynx.Cli.exe from Lynx-1.11.0-win-x64.zip, with its appsettings.json (online tablebase off, 1 thread)

notes: Built 2026-09-26 by adding nine families to pool-E. Pool-E's nine anchors, conditions and games are unchanged, so every pool-E game is also a pool-F game. pool-E is archived verbatim at pool-2026-09-E.json.

Removed 2026-09-26 after the first night, under the rule registered in pool_f_prediction.md: Priessnitz 2.0 lost on time in 230 of its 746 games at 10+0.1 here, and Onyx 2.0 implied ratings for Sgurr 407 to 486 above the solve on the other sixteen. Its binary reports its author as 'Dylan (with Claude)', which suggests it is a different engine from the Onyx 2.0 CCRL rated. Their games stay in the folder but are left out of solves.

Why more families: on pool-E the anchors implied ratings for Sgurr about 52 Elo apart beyond sampling noise, which left about +/-35 systematic on an absolute rating from nine families. Gains between versions were the same against every engine within noise, so this is about the absolute number, not the gaps. Eighteen families should bring it to about +/-25.

The new nine come from the live CCRL Blitz list of 2026-09-26: single-CPU ratings within +/-12, an official Windows build of exactly the rated version, and between them they fill pool-E's gaps (nothing from 3087 to 3231, nothing above 3362). The pool now runs 3087 to 3438, nine families either side of 3311.

Each build is the fastest one without AVX-512, as for pool-E. Every binary reports the rated version via `id name`, supports Hash, runs one thread and passed testing/engine_gate.py. Onyx 2.0 has its own book switched on by default, so `options` switches it off.

Not usable: Marvin 6.3.0 (its release has no Windows build), Expositor 4WR02 and Toga IV 1.1 (no homepage on CCRL), Isa 4.5 (no releases), Little Goliath Evolution 3.16, Protej 0.6.8, DanaSah 9.1 and Orion 1.1 (own websites only, not checked). Jet 1.2, Simbelmyne 1.10.0 and StockNemo 5.7.0.0 failed the rules gate on pool-D; Pedantic and Stash as for pool-E.

Adjudication was tested and rejected. Replayed on 8,168 pool-D games, resign adjudication (3 moves at 1000cp, both engines agreeing) saved 8% of time but turned 22 Sgurr draws into losses; draw adjudication saved 1% and turned 28 Sgurr wins into draws. A version-dependent bias is not worth 8%.
Time control stays 10+0.1. A CCRL-equivalent control (about 1'+0.6" here) would cost about six times as much per game and could not resolve a medium gain in a night.
A version's first run uses opening seed 1; a run that carries on takes a new seed so no opening is replayed.
